industry: Mortgage lenders, brokers and loan officers (purchase, refinance, VA/FHA, HELOC/cash-out, reverse); brief notes on adjacent financial mail
words_and_claims_to_avoid: Any rate without the APR equally prominent (Reg Z 1026.24(c)); 'as low as' rates without the APR and terms.
Trigger terms (down payment %, number of payments/term, payment amount, finance charge) without the required down payment, terms and APR disclosures (1026.24(d)).
'Fixed' for a loan that isn't fixed for its full term; comparisons to the consumer's current payment that aren't apples-to-apples (1026.24(i)).

Government look: eagles, seals, 'VA/FHA/HUD approved', 'government program', 'official notice', or naming the consumer's current lender without a clear non-affiliation statement (1026.24(i); Reg N; 39 USC 3001(h)).
'Pre-approved', 'approved instantly', 'poor credit OK', 'guaranteed approval' unless true; prescreened mail must make a firm offer of credit with FCRA notices (GOLD-013, 018).
'Could save you tens of thousands', '$35,000 average' (GOLD-001, 003) without substantiation from the lender's own data.
'Counselor' for a commercial lender (1026.24(i)(5)); 'tax-free money' / 'never lose your home' for reverse mortgages.
'Easy / push-button mortgage' framing that minimizes a major debt (Rocket 2016 backlash; style caution, not law).
Images or words that suggest a protected group would be denied or get worse terms (Reg B 1002.4(b), amended 2026).
compliance_notes: TILA/Reg Z 1026.24 (closed-end) and 1026.16 (HELOC): APR with any rate; trigger-term disclosures; payment amounts must say taxes/insurance not included if so (1026.24(f)); prohibited misleading terms (1026.24(i)).

Reg N (MAP Rule, 12 CFR 1014.3): bans misrepresenting rates, fees, payments, government affiliation, preapproval/likelihood of approval, the consumer's ability to get a loan, or that the ad is from the consumer's current lender.

CFPB 2020 consent orders against six VA-focused lenders (Sovereign, Prime Choice, Go Direct, PHLoans.com, Hypotec, Service 1st) for deceptive mail: misleading rates, implied VA/government affiliation, missing disclosures; penalties $50k-$645k.

Reverse mortgages: CFPB 2015 found ads created false impressions of a government benefit, 'no risk', and staying in the home for life. Don't use FHA/HUD logos or imply endorsement; disclose it's a loan that must be repaid and that taxes, insurance and upkeep are required. Some states add rules (e.g., NY restrictions on 'government insured' claims; confirm).

FCRA prescreened offers: firm offer of credit, prescreen opt-out notice (short and long form). Homebuyers Privacy Protection Act (P.L. 119-36, effective Mar 5 2026) restricts trigger-lead reports unless there's consent or an existing relationship and a firm offer.

ECOA/Reg B 1002.4(b) as amended (91 FR 21668, eff. July 21 2026): no oral/written statements or visual images that would lead a reasonable person to think credit would be denied or worse on a prohibited basis (race, sex, age, etc.); encouraging a group (e.g., veterans) isn't by itself discouragement of others. Fair Housing Act 3605 also covers mortgage lending.
SAFE Act / state rules: show company and individual NMLS IDs on ads; many states require license numbers and an Equal Housing Lender/Opportunity statement or logo.
RESPA Section 8: co-marketing with agents/builders at fair market value; no referral kickbacks.

Adjacent financial mail in the gold set (debt relief, tax prep, advisors, bank account bonuses) has its own rules (TSR for debt relief, SEC Marketing Rule/FINRA 2210 for advisors, Reg DD for deposit bonuses). Not researched this run - flag for a separate playbook.
standing_rules: Emotion-agnostic: fear, joy, pride, status, relief, nostalgia are all options; the client chooses.
Every angle and combo carries a sell-the-outcome line.
Unverified (agency/vendor-only) results are labeled; never quote them as fact on a card.
No age/demographic angle unless a cited source supports it for this industry; even then, check Fair Housing / ECOA before using it in housing or credit.

emotion_by_offer_conflicts.conflict: Gold VA cards with flags/Iwo Jima and 'could save tens of thousands' (GOLD-001, 002) vs Reg N/Reg Z and CFPB 2020 VA orders
emotion_by_offer_conflicts.resolution: Law wins: drop government-styled imagery, add non-affiliation statement, substantiate or remove savings claims.

emotion_by_offer_conflicts.conflict: Gold 'poor credit OK / approved instantly / pre-approved in 5 minutes' (GOLD-013, 018) vs Reg N and FCRA
emotion_by_offer_conflicts.resolution: Law wins: only true, specific preapproval language; firm-offer rules for prescreened mail.

emotion_by_offer_conflicts.conflict: Gold reverse-mortgage '$35,000 average' / 'MORE MONEY' (GOLD-003) vs CFPB 2015 findings
emotion_by_offer_conflicts.resolution: Law and verified study win: explain, don't hype; substantiate any average with own data.

emotion_by_offer_conflicts.conflict: Bertrand et al. (photo of a woman raised take-up) vs Reg B 2026 imagery standard
emotion_by_offer_conflicts.resolution: Law wins: people imagery is fine but must not imply who gets credit; use the study's stronger, safer lesson (one example loan > four).
No hard rule; empowerment preferred for big debts (style caution, backlash documented).
